limitations: The study cannot prove that daylighting actually causes students to learn more or perform better, only establishes correlation.
Less detailed analysis for Seattle and Fort Collins districts, increasing the probability of unaccounted factors invalidating results.
Limited information about student and school characteristics in Fort Collins, increasing likelihood of unknown confounding variables.
Modest range of window conditions in Fort Collins, potentially underreporting the full effect of window area.
Daylight variable in Fort Collins was based on expected illumination levels rather than actual observations throughout the school year, due to resource constraints.
The study did not account for daylight exposure outside of the classroom when considering its impact on health and behavior.
